Definition: from a presumed derivative of G3199; to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind:--imagine, (pre-)meditate.
BiblicalUsage: Meletao means to meditate, to turn a thing over in the mind until it takes hold. 1 Timothy 4:15 commands Timothy to meditate upon these things and give himself wholly to them, that his profiting may appear to all, and Acts 4:25 quotes the psalm asking why the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe meditation is a choice of what to turn over: truth that profits, or vain things that rage against God.
